title: Inkling 2 Small Automation Within the Vendor's Limits
summary: Inkling 2 small automation uses one trigger, one model call, and checked output. You'll understand the setup process, what limits exist, and common fixes.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Is Inkling 2 Small free to use? Not documented in the material this article draws on, so treat it as unconfirmed. Read the vendor's pricing page and note the date you read it.


A free tier that exists on paper can still carry usage caps that stop a flow midway, so confirm the caps too.


Can Inkling 2 Small run automations without code? Not documented here. The vendor's docs are the only source that can settle it.


If no-code triggers aren't listed there, assume you'll need a small amount of glue code or a separate workflow tool to start the model call. Plan the one-trigger, one-call, one-check flow around that.


Does Inkling 2 Small have an API? Not documented here, so confirm it before building.


Look for an API reference page, authentication instructions and a stated rate limit. If any of the three is missing, you have no basis for scheduling unattended runs, and a flow that depends on them will fail without warning.


How often do Inkling 2 Small limits change? No change schedule is documented here, so assume **limits can change at any time** . That's why the docs-and-pricing check needs a recurring date.


Compare the current page with your last saved copy. If a limit has moved, the flow can break even though nothing on your side changed.


### What should I use if Inkling 2 Small is too limited?


Pick a model whose vendor documents the limits you need, then rerun the same dated check on it. Current options built for high-volume, low-latency work include Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.


Mistral Small 4 is another choice if you want a small general model.


Keep the same narrow design, one trigger, one call and one checked output. Then swapping the model changes one step and leaves the rest of the flow alone.
